MINUTES
  MALIBU PLANNING COMMISSION
  REGULAR MEETING
  NOVEMBER 7, 2022
  TELECONFERENCED VARIOUS LOCATIONS
  -

  6:30 P.M.

The following meeting was held pursuant to the Governor’s Executive Orders N-25-20 and N-29-
20 and fully teleconferenced from various locations during the coronavirus disease (COVID- 19)
pandemic.

CALL TO ORDER

  Chair Smith called the meeting to order at 6:3 1 p.m.

ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance by the Recording Secretary:

  PRESENT: Chair Dennis R. Smith, Vice Chair John Mazza and Commissioners Kraig Hill,
  Jeffrey Jennings and Mark Wetton

  ALSO PRESENT: Trevor Rusin, Interim City Attorney; Richard Mollica, Planning
  Director; Adrian Fernandez, Assistant Planning Director; Troy Spayd, Assistant Public
  Works Director; Jessica Thompson, Senior Planner; Raneika Brooks, Senior Planner; Tyler
  Eaton, Associate Planner; Adam Pisarkiewicz, Contract Planner; Courtney McCammon,
  City Biologist; Lauren Doyel, Contract Coastal Engineer and Geotechnical Reviewer;
  Johana Valencia, Planning Technician; and Rebecca Evans, Recording Secretary

APPROVAL OF AGENDA

MOTION  Vice Chair Mazza moved and Commissioner Hill seconded a motion to approve
  the agenda as recommended by staff and to hear Item No. 5.B. prior to Item No.
  5.A.

  The question was called and the motion carried unanimously.

REPORT ON POSTING OF AGENDA

  Recording Secretary Evans reported that the agenda for the meeting was properly posted
  on October 28, 2022.

ITEM 1  CEREMONIAL/PRESENTATIONS
  None.
   Malibu Planning Commission

ITEM 2.A.  PUBLIC COMMENTS

  Alexander Hakim requested the Planning Commission consider scheduling a
  Special Meeting to hear the proposed Malibu Inn Motel with the current Planning
  Commission composition.

  Lonnie Gordon expressed concern regarding the use of known carcinogens on
  wooden utility poles within the City and diesel fueled emergency generators used
  by Southern California Edison. which produce exhaust containing chemicals
  known to cause cancer.

  Jo Drummond stated the water flow proposed for the Malibu Inn Motel
  development was considerably higher than current use and questioned how it was
  approved by the Regional Water Quality Control Board at four times the fixture
  count and flow.

  Steven Hakim stated the Malibu Inn Motel application went above and beyond what
  was requested by the Regional Water Quality Control Board and asked the Planning
  Commission to select a date for a Special Planning Commission meeting.

ITEM 2.B.  COMMISSION I STAFF COMMENTS

  Commissioner Hill noted a brief power outage in Big Rock prior to the meeting.
  The coastal overlook in Coastal Development Permit No. 21-022 was referred to as
  Dolphin Point Overlook. An area known locally as Figment Cove was titled
  Maritime Rocks by Mountains Recreation and Conservation Authority. He asked if
  the City had authority for naming or if the Mountains Recreation and Conservation
  Authority had final authority on name selection. Commissioner Hill questioned the
  language used in staff reports for discretionary requests. He asked staff for the cause
  of the low, loud rumble over the weekend, an update on the cause of the delays on
  the Trancas Canyon Bridge construction, and whether utilities had an exemption
  that allowed treatment of poles with carcinogenic materials.

  Vice Chair Mazza wished all City Council candidates well and congratulated them
  on their effort regardless of election results.

  Commissioner Wetton also questioned the cause of the loud rumble over the
  weekend. He expressed condolences to the Bulow family on the loss of Andreas
  and Marco in a tragic accident as well as the family members of the traffic fatality
  at Point Mugu over the weekend.

  Chair Smith offered congratulations to Senior Planner Thompson and to his son on
  their upcoming weddings on November 11, 2022 and belated congratulations to
  Associate Planner Eaton on his marriage.
   Malibu Planning Commission
  Minutes of November 7, 2022
  Page 3 of II

Vice Chair Mazza asked to dedicate the meeting in memory of Andreas and Marco
Bulow. He offered congratulations to Senior Planner Thompson, Associate Planner
Eaton and Chair Smith’s son on their weddings.

In response to Commissioner Hill, Planning Director Mollica stated there were
exemptions to allow for utility pole replacements with weather-treated materials.He
noted Malibu did not have a naming rights requirement for non-City owned parks
or trails. There was a design issue with the Trancas Bridge sign. After redesign,
plans would be reviewed to ensure compliance with conditions of approval.

In response to Commissioners Hill and Wetton, Planning Director Mollica
confirmed a loud rumble was heard from Malibu to La Jolla and stated he would
look into the cause.

Planning Director Mollica stated the City Council’s Administration and Finance
Subcommittee would hold a special meeting to consider additional funding for
contract planners. Staff were identifying a time and date for a Zoning Ordinance
Revisions and Code Enforcement Subcommittee meeting to finalize discussion
regarding the Temporary Use Permit item due to a power outage within Malibu
near the end of the prior meeting.

Planning Director Mollica noted three large items would head to Planning
Commission in addition to ongoing residential developments and continuances. He
asked for guidance on the Commission’s preference for scheduling large Public
Works and capital improvements projects; the Malibu Inn Motel (which was
previously heard as a special meeting due to the number of public speakers); and
Phase I of the Malibu Middle and High School project. The caveat was that the
specific plan for Malibu Middle and High School was still with California Coastal
Commission, and he recommended hearing that item after provided with feedback
on requested changes. He requested Commission direction on whether these items
should be heard at regular or special meetings.

Commissioner Hill would like to consider late January for hearing one of the larger
items. However, he expressed doubt regarding the Memorandum of Understanding
amendment and did not believe the Malibu Inn Motel would be ready for a hearing
within the next month or two.

Assistant City Attorney Rusin clarified that the Commission could not discuss
particulars of any issue, just whether or not to schedule large items for a special or
regular meeting.

Commissioner Jennings asked for confirmation on whether the November 1 7, 2022
tentative meeting date was still being considered for a special meeting on Malibu
   Malibu Planning Commission
  Minutes of November 7, 2022
  Page4ofll

 Inn Motel.

 Recording Secretary Evans confirmed the November 17, 2022 tentative date was
 no longer under consideration for a special meeting due to the City Council’s
 continuance of the Conditional Use Permit Amendment for Aviator Nation and
 legal notice requirements.

Vice Chair Mazza requested a report from Planning Director Mollica with more
information on the backlog of projects and upcoming large projects which would
be brought to the Planning Commission. He expressed willingness to add special
meetings as needed. He asked staff ifthe Trancas Bridge project would be on hold
for the full rainy season.

Contract Coastal Engineer and Geotechnical Reviewer Doyel informed the
Planning Commission that California Department of Transportation did not hit
bedrock at the pile depth anticipated and the project would require re-engineering.

Commissioner Wetton noticed the temporary dam to contain debris headed toward
the ocean at Trancas Bridge was recently removed so it appeared likely California
Department of Transportation would wait until the rainy season ended.

Chair Smith noted many residents were upset about the Hosted Short-Term Rental
decision and the California Coastal Commission stated Malibu needed more visitor
accommodations. It seemed the motel project might contribute to meeting visitor
accommodation needs. The State could litigate against the City of Malibu regarding
the Housing Element. He recommended moving forward on the Accessory
Dwelling Unit Ordinance to avoid imposition of State mandates.

Vice Chair Mazza stated the Housing Element Law was under the City Council’s
purview and while the City was required to zone for specific uses, there was not a
requirement to build.

Commissioner Hill noted California Coastal Commission could require more short-
term rentals than previously allowed in Malibu and increased construction of
accessory dwelling units could also offset housing needs.

Planning Director Mollica stated staff would investigate special meeting dates after
the new year and provide a report on upcoming large projects and routine
applications heading to Planning Commission.

Chair Smith noted that the Malibu Middle and High School project would already
be six months behind if heard in December 2022 and costs were rising with time.

Vice Chair Mazza stated the cost of lumber dropped fifty percent over the last few
   Malibu Planning Commission

  months, which may help offset costs for Malibu Middle and High School campus.
